knowledge-base.name: research-rag
knowledge-base.description: Guidelines for using the workspace-scoped research RAG: when to use it, how to find quality sources, chunking expectations, query strategies, and anti-patterns to avoid.

when-to-use.use-case: Unfamiliar library or framework — official docs, README, migration guides
Security patterns — OWASP, CVE advisories, auth/crypto specs (RFC, NIST)
Architecture decisions — compare approaches before proposing one
Compliance requirements — GDPR, HIPAA, PCI-DSS spec sections
Algorithm research — arxiv papers, academic surveys
Third-party API integration — vendor docs, SDK changelogs

not-for.item: Reading project code — use POST http://127.0.0.1:8612/search scope=codebase or direct file reads
Debugging a specific error — read stack traces and code directly
Anything already covered by the ClaudeBoost knowledge bases (POST http://127.0.0.1:8612/search scope=knowledge)
General questions answerable from training data

tier.name: A
tier.label: auto-trust
tier.description: High-signal, authoritative sources. Auto-include in candidate list.
tier.domains: arxiv.org, github.com, docs.python.org, docs.rs, pkg.go.dev, crates.io, *.readthedocs.io, developer.mozilla.org (MDN), docs.microsoft.com, developer.apple.com, cloud.google.com/docs, docs.aws.amazon.com, learn.microsoft.com, peps.python.org, tc39.es, w3.org, ietf.org, nist.gov, owasp.org

tier.name: B
tier.label: include-by-default
tier.description: Generally reliable. Include unless user says skip.
tier.domains: stackoverflow.com, dev.to, engineering.*.com (official vendor engineering blogs), blog.*.io (if from recognized open source project authors), css-tricks.com, smashingmagazine.com, web.dev, freecodecamp.org

tier.name: C
tier.label: show-ask
tier.description: Variable quality. Show to user with label; do not auto-select.
tier.domains: medium.com, hashnode.dev, substack.com, personal blogs, dev.to posts by unknown authors, reddit.com (r/programming etc.), hackernoon.com

tier.name: skip
tier.label: exclude
tier.description: Exclude silently. Do not surface to user.
tier.signals: Paywalled content (paywall detected in fetched text), Social media (twitter.com, linkedin.com, facebook.com), SEO aggregator spam (thin content, keyword-stuffed titles), Results that are 100% ads or marketing copy, Sites requiring login to read content

acceptance-criteria.description: Standard thresholds for rating research coverage confidence. Use these in research-brief.md Coverage Summary.

level.name: High
level.threshold: 3 or more Tier A sources covering this angle, published within 2 years
level.or: 2 Tier A sources + explicit consensus (no contradictions found)

level.name: Medium
level.threshold: 1-2 Tier A sources, OR 2+ Tier B sources with no contradictions
level.note: Sufficient for most implementation decisions. Flag if topic is security-critical.

level.name: Low
level.threshold: Fewer than 2 reputable sources, OR sources with significant contradictions
level.action: Note this explicitly in research-brief.md Gaps section. Do not suppress low-confidence findings — surface them so implementers can decide.

level.name: None
level.threshold: Zero Tier A/B sources found after 1 retry
level.action: Mark angle as "No authoritative source found" in brief. Do not fabricate or infer coverage from Tier C sources alone.

decision-tree.rule: URL ends with .pdf → use PDF ingestion path (chunk_pdf_url)
URL returns Content-Type: application/pdf → same PDF path
GitHub blob/raw URL (github.com/*/blob/* or raw.githubusercontent.com) → HTML path (renders as page)
arxiv.org/abs/* → HTML path (abstract page); arxiv.org/pdf/* → PDF path

pdf-vs-url.pdf-caveats: PyMuPDF extracts text reliably from most PDFs. Known limitations: - Image-only scanned PDFs: no text extracted (pages skipped, result count = 0) - Math formulas: extracted as plain text, symbols may be garbled - Multi-column layouts: text order may be incorrect If chunk count is unexpectedly low, check if the PDF is scanned/image-based.

chunking-guidelines.split-strategy: HTML/Markdown: split on H2/H3 heading boundaries first, then paragraph breaks if section exceeds 512 tokens. PDF: split on detected section headings (all-caps lines, numbered headings), then paragraphs.
chunking-guidelines.minimum-chunk: 40 tokens — chunks below this are discarded as noise
chunking-guidelines.code-blocks: Preserved intact; not split mid-block even if they exceed max_tokens
chunking-guidelines.quality-signal: If POST http://127.0.0.1:8612/index_research returns fewer than 5 chunks for a source, the page was likely: (a) blocked/paywalled, (b) image-only PDF, (c) a redirect page with no content. Investigate before trusting that source.

url-retry-strategy.trigger: URL returns fewer than 5 chunks AND domain is Tier A or B

actions.action: Check if URL redirects — follow the final URL and re-index that instead
Try the root domain docs page instead of the deep-linked page
If PDF: check for an HTML version of the same document
Hard cap: 1 retry per URL. If still under 5 chunks, mark as "sparse" in brief and continue

url-retry-strategy.note: A sparse Tier A source is still worth keeping — even 2-3 chunks from official docs beats 20 chunks from a blog post.

query-strategies.principle: Write specific, concept-level queries — not broad topics
query-strategies.multi-query: For complex topics, run 2-3 narrow queries covering different aspects rather than one broad query. Example for OAuth2: - "OAuth2 PKCE flow authorization code" - "refresh token rotation security" - "OAuth2 state parameter CSRF protection"
query-strategies.combine-with-codebase: Research RAG answers "how does X work". Project codebase RAG answers "where is X used in this project". Use both when implementing something new in an existing codebase.
query-strategies.score-threshold: rag_search results include a similarity score (0.0–1.0). Treat results by tier: - score >= 0.7 : high confidence — cite directly with file:line or source URL - score 0.6–0.69: moderate confidence — usable, but note uncertainty if citing specifically - score < 0.6 : weak match — do NOT cite as fact; verify by reading the source first Agents MUST NOT cite a file:line or claim a source says something based solely on a result with score below 0.6. Read and confirm the content before citing.

query-refinement-playbook.description: When initial search returns fewer than 3 Tier A/B sources for an angle, escalate specificity in one retry. Hard cap: 1 retry per angle.

escalation-pattern.level: Start specific but not version-pinned — e.g. "React useEffect cleanup"
Add qualifier or context — e.g. "React useEffect cleanup async subscriptions"
Add version + specific API — e.g. "React 18 useEffect cleanup AbortController pattern"

example.attempt-2: OAuth2 PKCE authorization code flow security
example.attempt-3: OAuth2 PKCE SHA-256 code_verifier JavaScript implementation

example.attempt-2: PostgreSQL migration zero downtime blue-green deployment
example.attempt-3: PostgreSQL 15 schema migration backward compatible add column nullable

example.attempt-2: FastAPI dependency injection testing mock override
example.attempt-3: FastAPI 0.100 Depends override pytest integration test pattern

query-refinement-playbook.rule: Never retry more than once. If the refined query still returns no Tier A/B sources, note the gap in the research brief and continue. "No authoritative source found" is a valid finding.

workspace-scoping.rule: Research RAG is strictly per-task. Each task workspace gets its own ChromaDB instance at workspace/[task-id]/.rag-index/research/. It does NOT share data with: - The global ClaudeBoost RAG (agents/, knowledge/) - Other task workspaces - The project codebase index
workspace-scoping.workspace-path: Always pass the absolute path to the task workspace directory. Example: /path/to/ClaudeBoost/workspace/AUTH-42 The research index will be at workspace/AUTH-42/.rag-index/research/

anti-patterns.anti-pattern: Do not index a source and immediately trust rag_search results as ground truth. If the source is critical (security, compliance), read the actual document section to verify the chunk is accurate and not truncated mid-thought.
Do not index more than 20 URLs without user consent. Broad scrapes slow indexing and dilute search quality with irrelevant content.
Do not index 10+ pages from the same site without considering breadth. A single vendor's docs may not represent the full solution space.
Always check sources_failed and whether any source returned fewer than 5 chunks. Low chunk counts indicate a failed fetch, blocked page, or image-only PDF.
Research RAG supplements code reading; it does not replace it. Never skip reading the actual project code in favor of research results.
Research RAG is per-task and ephemeral. After a task is complete, the index is no longer maintained. Do not reuse research from a different task's workspace.

codebase-search-modes.description: POST http://127.0.0.1:8612/search scope=codebase has two modes. Choose based on what you need to find.

mode.name: vector
mode.usage: POST http://127.0.0.1:8612/search with scope="codebase", query="...", project_path="..."
mode.what-it-finds: Semantically similar code — functions, classes, and comments whose meaning is close to your query. Best for: "find the payment processing logic", "where is user authentication handled".

mode.name: graph
mode.usage: POST http://127.0.0.1:8612/search with scope="codebase", query="...", project_path="...", mode="graph"
mode.what-it-finds: Vector seeds PLUS structural neighbours — files that import from, inherit from, or are called by the seed files. Best for: understanding a module's callers/dependencies, finding everything that changes when you modify a file, tracing a data flow across file boundaries.
mode.how-it-works: 1. Runs normal vector search to get seed results 2. Looks up each seed file in graph.db (SQLite, built at index time by rag_index_project) 3. Fetches depth-1 structural neighbours (imports, inherits edges) 4. Merges and deduplicates; neighbour chunks scored slightly below their seed

edge-types.edge: import/require/use statements parsed directly from AST
class A extends/inherits B, parsed from AST

mode.requires: Project must have been indexed with rag_index_project (graph.db built automatically). If graph.db does not exist, mode=graph silently falls back to vector results.
mode.when-to-prefer: - "What files import this module?" → mode=graph - "Show me everything that changes when I modify class Foo" → mode=graph - "What does this function do?" → mode=vector (semantic is better here)

codebase-search-modes.tier-4b-auto-augmentation: POST http://127.0.0.1:8612/context automatically applies graph augmentation to Tier 4 (codebase) results when a graph index exists for the project. This is transparent — no extra parameter needed. Structural neighbours of the top-3 vector seeds are appended within a token budget.
